title: SRE 15min triage and soft backfill playbook (draft)
content:
Summary

This is a lightweight runbook for the first 15 minutes of an infra incident that manifests as degraded inference capacity or latency spikes attributed to GPU node failures or hot I/O issues. Focus: fast triage, partial traffic shaping, and a soft backfill procedure that brings capacity up incrementally to avoid noisy neighbor effects and cold-cache storms.

Intent and scope
- Fast stabilization: stop user-visible error amplification within 15 minutes.
- Minimal blast radius: prefer routing and throttling over wide-evacuations when possible.
- Soft backfill: add capacity in small batches and warm KV/prefix caches to avoid regressions in latency and throughput.
- This is a draft for oncall use; items labeled "TODO" are design questions for post-incident review.

When to use this playbook
- Multiple pods in a node/pool enter CrashLoopBackoff or OOM within a short window.
- Sustained token-processing latency increases >2x baseline for >=5 minutes.
- Error rate (5xx) > 1% and correlates with specific GPU pool or AZ.
- Immediate hardware replacement not possible (no spare cartridges available).

First 0-5 minutes: rapid assessment (15-min triage window)
- Caller (pager) to populate incident header in Slack channel and incident doc. Use template: "SRE: [region/pool] degraded - latency spike/error increase".
- Run quick queries (one-liners):
  - kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=<pool> --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
  - kubectl describe node <node> | egrep -A4 "Allocatable|Capacity|Conditions"
  - curl -s "https://metrics.redwood.ai/api/v1/query?query=rate(inference_5xx_total[1m])" | jq .
- Identify scope: single node vs multi-node vs cross-AZ. Check load balancer routing and recent deploys (last 10m).
- If deploy in last 10m -> rollback flag = true. Call owner of PR.

Decision tree (quick):
- If single node with hardware fault and immediate replacement available -> follow GPU replacment hot-swap steps (see section below).
- If multi-node across AZs -> consider traffic shaping to other clusters/regions and open multi-cluster failover playbook.
- If single pool degraded but not fully down -> proceed with soft backfill (below).

0-15 minutes: containment and partial mitigation
1) Rate-limit and circuit-break:
  - Apply per-route soft rate-limit: UPDATE routing-control service: set token_per_sec throttle for affected pool to 60% of baseline.
  - Enable local 429-responses (rather than 500s) for non-critical customers if configured.
  - Rationale: early shedding prevents queue accumulation and OOMs, buys time for controlled capacity add.
2) Route away ephemeral traffic:
  - Use smart routing to divert new sessions to compatible model variants in adjacent pools/regions.
  - Use the console to increase fallback weight to warm pool by +20% (monitor errors).
3) Signal ops and procurement if physical replacement required:
  - If hardware suspected, call hardware-oncall and log required spare type.

Soft backfill procedure (safe capacity add)
- Goal: add nodes in small groups (2-3 GPUs) and warm caches before moving large fractions of traffic.
- Preconditions: autoscaler healthy, image versions pinned, capacity quotas available.
- Steps:
  1. Provision small instance set: request 1-2 nodes tagged with pool=<affected>-temp via infra-autoscaler (CLI: infractl capacity add --pool <pool> --count 1 --labels temp-backfill).
  2. Wait until nodes are Ready. kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node -l label=temp-backfill --timeout=10m
  3. Start model runtime but keep routing weight at 0 (do not accept production traffic).
  4. Warm caches: run synthetic warmup traffic from load-test agent: curl -XPOST https://loadtest.redwood.ai/warm?pool=<pool>&model=<model>&prefixes=seedsetA
     - Warmup guidance: small fanout, respect per-token rate limits; aim to prefill KV caches and tokenization caches.
  5. Observe latency and error rates for the warmup group for 3-5 minutes. If stable, incrementally increase routing weight by 10-20% every 2 minutes.
  6. If any regression (p95 latency > baseline * 1.5 or errors > 0.5%), immediately reduce weight to previous safe level and investigate (look at GPU metrics, PCIe errors).
- Notes: Avoid adding >20% of previously-handled capacity in any single backfill wave.

GPU hot-swap quick checklist (when you have a spare cartridge)
- Safety: ensure node is cordoned and workloads drained (soft) before physical swap. Coordinate with datacenter/hardware ops.
- Steps (oncall):
  1. kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
  2. Verify pods rescheduled in other nodes; watch for eviction turbulence.
  3. Ship hardware team the node id and failure symptoms. Provide serial logs: journalctl -u driver.service | tail -n 200
  4. After swap and power cycle, run pcie self-test and nvlink check script (infra/scripts/gpu-health-check.sh).
  5. Uncordon node: kubectl uncordon <node> and watch pod placement.
  6. Reintegrate capacity using soft backfill steps (warm caches) rather than immediately restoring full routing weight.

Observability and signals to watch (minimal set)
- latency: inference_latency_p95, inference_latency_p50, inference_queue_length
- errors: inference_5xx_rate, grpc_abort_rate
- infra: node_gpu_mem_utilization, pci_errors_total, gpu_thermal_throttle_count
- scheduler: pod_eviction_rate, kube_node_status_condition
- business: active_sessions_by_customer (for targeted shedding)

Escalation and communication
- If containment fails within 15 minutes -> page SRE lead and infra engineering.
- Post first-15: create incident doc with timeline (start, triage actions, mitigation steps, owners).
- Use standardized updates: every 10 minutes during active incident (short bulleted: action -> owner -> next check).

Rollback and cleanup
- If we increased fallback weights/routing changes, record exact deltas and revert when cluster stable.
- Remove temp nodes after 30 minutes of stable operation or per post-incident plan. Command: infractl capacity remove --label=temp-backfill --dry-run then execute.
- Sanitize logs and mark suspicious nodes for deeper hardware inspection.

Post-incident (within 48h) checklist
- Run a lightweight postmortem: owner, timeline (with 1-min resolution for first 15), detected root cause hypothesis, and action items (RCA vs operational improvements).
- Required follow-ups:
  - Add metrics instrumentation if missing (e.g., per-GPU PCIe error counters).
  - Update playbook to remove ambiguity (TODO: exact thresholds for warmup and weight increments).
  - Create ticket for hardware spare policy review if hardware replacement was limiting.

Open questions / TODOs (for this draft)
- Threshold tuning: set explicit values for p95 degradation and error thresholds for auto-shedding.
- Warmup tooling: do we have a standard seedset that reflects production distribution? Who maintains it?
- Automation: can we automate the add->warmup->promote cycle in infractl with safety gates? (preferably yes)

Appendix: quick commands cheat sheet
- Check pods: kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep <pool>
- Cordon + drain: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
- Wait for node ready: kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/<node> --timeout=10m
- Add capacity (infractl): infractl capacity add --pool <pool> --count 1 --labels temp-backfill
- Remove temp nodes: infractl capacity remove --label=temp-backfill

Notes from last rehearsal (2024-10-22)
- Warmup synthetic traffic must use the same tokenization config as production otherwise cache miss behavior is unrealistic.
- Observability gap: we did not have per-tenant p99 which made customer impact assessment slow.

Slack update template (first 15min)
- "SRE: [pool=<pool>] detected latency spike and 5xx increase at <time>. Running 15-min triage: rate-limiting non-critical routes and starting soft backfill. Owner: @Aisha. Next update in 10m unless escalated."

End of draft.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-06 created by Aisha Patel (initial outline)
- 2024-11-15 added soft backfill increments section (Marco Chen)
- 2025-02-18 updated observability signals and cheat-sheet (Lena Ortiz)
